title: peer_nodes_excluding: non-deterministic node selection for multi-device users
description: StatusResponse::peer_nodes_excluding() (kith-tslocal/src/lib.rs line 130) deduplicates users by user_id but picks whichever node appears first during HashMap iteration, which is non-deterministic. The function is called in discovery (kithd/src/discovery.rs:352) to build the contact list. A user's two nodes (laptop + phone) yield an arbitrary dns_name for the mailbox_host. The doc comment says 'caller should not rely on which node is chosen' but does not say what the caller should do instead. In practice, if a peer has two nodes and the wrong one is selected, Peer/deliver will fail and the outbox retry loop will keep hitting the wrong host. Consequence: persistent delivery failures for multi-device peers are silent, not surfaced to the owner. The risk is not a crash but a correctness hole in the contact discovery flow.
